name: V-Y advancement / vermilion advancement
lead: Vermilion advancement is a group of surgical techniques that move or advance the pink lip tissue, the vermilion, to rebuild or enlarge it. In the literature it is mostly a reconstructive method, for example after tumour removal from the lip, while in cosmetic surgery it is discussed as a way to increase pink lip show [1][2][3].

A 1996 review of cosmetic lip surgery presented aesthetic guidelines on Cupid's bow, upper lip length and projection [1]. Reconstructive reports describe modified Goldstein-type bilateral vermilion flaps after Mohs surgery for lip squamous cell carcinoma [2] and a vermilion advancement flap with a facial artery musculomucosal flap after buccal mucosa tumour resection [3].
Little published research covers vermilion advancement as a purely cosmetic operation.

paras: Advancement flaps slide adjacent mucosa or skin into a defect or toward a desired border. In lip reconstruction after tumour removal, authors describe bilateral flaps that expand tissue to cover vermilion defects [2]. Other reports pair vermilion advancement with additional flaps for defects of the oral commissure [3][4][5].

Evidence is limited to surgical case reports and reconstruction series [2][3][4][5]. A 1996 review set out aesthetic principles for cosmetic lip surgery [1]. A registered trial compares techniques in unilateral cleft lip repair, a related but distinct area [6].

card.summary: Flap surgery that moves pink lip tissue; mostly reconstructive, with little cosmetic research.
card.note: Cosmetic use has little published evidence.

quick.overview:
Vermilion advancement slides lip tissue to rebuild or enlarge the pink lip. Most reports concern reconstruction after cancer surgery.

Cosmetic use is thinly documented.
quick.mechanism: Flaps of lip tissue are advanced toward the lip border to restore or increase vermilion.
quick.risks: Surgical scarring and asymmetry are general concerns; cosmetic-specific data are not published in the sources reviewed.
